g.text: RAG grounds LLMs in retrieved docs
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for
improving the factual accuracy of large language models by grounding
responses in retrieved documents (Gao et al., 2023).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=1) Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving the factual accuracy of large language models by grounding responses in retrieved documents (Gao et al., 2023).

g.text: vote on document-ID agreement, not answer freq
This motivates a new aggregation strategy: rather than voting on answer
frequency, we vote on document-ID agreement among evidence-valid responses.
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) This motivates a new aggregation strategy: rather than voting on answer frequency, we vote on document-ID agreement among evidence-valid responses.

g.text: We propose Citation-Consistent Voting (CCV), a training-free method that
aggregates answers based on document-ID agreement rather than answer
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) We propose Citation-Consistent Voting (CCV), a training-free method that aggregates answers based on document-ID agreement rather than answer frequency.

g.text: filter -> map to invariant doc IDs -> pick top score
CCV filters responses for evidence validity (ensuring the answer is grounded
in the cited document), maps citations to permutation-invariant document
IDs, and selects the answer with the highest citation-consistency score.
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=0) CCV filters responses for evidence validity (ensuring the answer is grounded in the cited document), maps citations to permutation-invariant document IDs, and selects the answer with the highest citation-consistency score.

g.title: N13 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose Citation-Consistent Voting, a training-free inference-time method for permutation-robust RAG that exploits citation structure for answer aggregation.
